items.title: Bangladesh could change cricket forever, again
items.summary: Every decade, Bangladesh finds a way to bend the arc of world cricket -- not through continuous dominance, but through a seismic upset

items.title: History within reach in Darwin as Bangladesh corner Australia
items.summary: The Tigers' triumph over New Zealand in Mount Maunganui in 2022 and the West Indies’ stunning Brisbane victory over Australia in 2024 remain among the defining Test upsets of the modern era. Now Bangladesh have the chance to add another chapter to that history.

items.title: Day 3 in Darwin: Key stats and records
items.summary: Bangladesh’s commanding performance in Darwin has produced a host of notable milestones as the Tigers put themselves in a strong position against Australia after Day 3.

items.title: Miraz focused on getting Australia out ‘as soon as possible’
items.summary: Asked how many runs Bangladesh would want Australia to score before setting a target, Miraz laughed off the question and said the visitors were not looking that far ahead.

items.title: Shanto ‘focused on process, not result’ despite being on top
items.summary: The Tigers entered the Test in Darwin hoping simply to play five days of competitive cricket, but three days into the match they find themselves in a commanding position after producing an impressive all-round performance.

items.title: Hazlewood sees Bangladesh blueprint for Australia
items.summary: Hazlewood believes the pitch remains good for batting but said Australia need to build pressure rather than simply attack.

items.title: Bangladesh chip away to keep famous victory in sight
items.summary: Hasan Mahmud claimed both Australia's openers while Mehidy Hasan Miraz followed a half-century with the key wicket of Steven Smith

items.title: Patience dictates Tanzid’s rare feat
items.summary: In only his second Test, Tanzid dictated proceedings with patience in one of the hardest places to score runs.

items.title: Tigers stay in control as Australia steady late in Darwin
items.summary: Australia reached 161 for four at stumps, still trailing Bangladesh by 67 runs with two days remaining. Green was unbeaten on 43 and Carey on 19, with the pair ensuring there was no further damage before the close.

items.title: Tanzid, Shanto and Mehidy keep Bangladesh in front after gripping day's play
items.summary: Australia had most of their success in a brief spell with the second new ball, but it's been Bangladesh most of the way otherwise

items.title: Smith was ready to walk off before DRS flat line
items.summary: Bangladesh were convinced Smith had edged behind early in his innings and the batter himself thought so too

items.title: Mahmud's 6 for 55 gives Bangladesh dream start
items.summary: Steven Smith waged a lone battle for Australia with 71 in 109 balls, but it was largely a sorry batting effort

items.title: Australia bat first in Darwin, Bangladesh play Ebadot and Mahmud
items.summary: There could be some early movement on offer with the new ball to test the home side's top order

items.title: Long wait over for Bangladesh and Darwin as Australia start their long run
items.summary: For the home side this is the start of a massive 12 months in Test cricket and they won't want to slip up early on

items.title: 'Bounce is the key' as Bangladesh look to rebound from 54 all out, says Shanto
items.summary: Najmul Hossain Shanto hinted that Bangladesh will field two spinners in Darwin despite the fast and bouncy conditions

items.title: Hazlewood keeps Boland out of Australia XI for first Test
items.summary: The home side named the XI that had been expected but Bangladesh will wait until the morning of the match to confirm their team

items.title: Taskin 'honoured' to play Test series in Australia, 14 years after first visit
items.summary: Bangladesh played their only Test series in the country in 2003
